title: Rigveda 9.48: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.48: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.48 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 685v-686r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.48.1-2 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 685v
translation.original_text:
1taṁ tvā̍ nṛ̱mṇāni̱ bibhra̍taṁ sa̱dhasthe̍ṣu ma̱ho di̱vaḥ | cāru̍ṁ sukṛ̱tyaye̍mahe ||
2saṁvṛ̍ktadhṛṣṇum u̱kthya̍m ma̱hāma̍hivrata̱m mada̍m | śa̱tam puro̍ ruru̱kṣaṇi̍m ||
translation.text:
1WITH sacrifice we seek to thee kind Cherisher of manly might In mansions of the lofty heavens;
2Gladdening crusher of the bold, ruling with very mighty sway, Destroyer of a hundred forts.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 685v (numbered 2v by the scribe) (OPenn image 686, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.46.3 ‹karma-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 686r (numbered 3r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.48.3 ‹rayim abhi rājānam sukrato›. Verses 9.48.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1tam | tvā | nṛmṇāni | vibhratam | sadha-stheṣu | mahaḥ | divaḥ | cārum | su-kṛtyayā | īmahe
2saṃvṛkta-dhṛṣṇum | ukthyam | mahāmahivratam | madam | śatam | puraḥ | rurukṣaṇim

translation.original_ref: RV 9.48.3-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 686r
translation.original_text:
3ata̍s tvā ra̱yim a̱bhi rājā̍naṁ sukrato di̱vaḥ | su̱pa̱rṇo a̍vya̱thir bha̍rat ||
4viśva̍smā̱ it sva̍r dṛ̱śe sādhā̍raṇaṁ raja̱stura̍m | go̱pām ṛ̱tasya̱ vir bha̍rat ||
5adhā̍ hinvā̱na i̍ndri̱yaṁ jyāyo̍ mahi̱tvam ā̍naśe | a̱bhi̱ṣṭi̱kṛd vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
translation.text:
3Hence, Sapient One! the Falcon, strong of wing, unwearied, brought thee down, Lord over riches, from the sky.
4That each may see the light, the Bird brought us the guard of Law, the Friend Of all, the speeder through the air.
5And now, sent forth, it hath attained to mighty power and majesty, Most active, ready to assist.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 686r (numbered 3r by the scribe) (OPenn image 686, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.48.3 ‹rayim abhi rājānam sukrato›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 686v (numbered 3v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.50.3 ‹-harim hinvanti adri-bhiḥ pavamānam›. Verses 9.48.3-5 end on this page; 9.48.3 begins on fol. 685v (numbered 2v by the scribe).
translation.edition_text:
3ataḥ | tvā | rayim | abhi | rājānam | sukrato itisu-krato | divaḥ | su-parṇaḥ | avyathiḥ | bharat
4viśvasmai | it | svaḥ | dṛśe | sādhāraṇam | rajaḥ-turam | gopām | ṛtasya | viḥ | bharat
5adha | hinvānaḥ | indriyam | jyāyaḥ | mahi-tvam | ānaśe | abhiṣṭi-kṛt | vi-carṣaṇiḥ
